summary: @servicetitan/launchdarkly-service 38.1.6 ships an obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches the Bun runtime and executes a hidden 727 KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-mangled _0xXXXX identifiers) and, on npm install, downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases for the detected platform/architecture, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes a sibling file math_init.js with the freshly downloaded Bun binary via execFileSync. math_init.js sits at the tarball root, is ~727 KB, carries a '// @bun @bun-cjs' header, and is heavily obfuscated (rotated numeric string-array n7gIxM, alphabet-substitution decoder hc1jfK9, 'with' statements used to defeat static parsers). The package.json 'files' manifest declares only ['dist','src'], so math_init.js is smuggled into the published tarball outside the declared file set and is only executed after preinstall pulls a second JS runtime unrelated to the package's advertised purpose (a LaunchDarkly React wrapper). The legitimate library code under dist/ is disjoint from this install-time surface, consistent with a hijacked-publisher release rather than the maintainer's normal output. Alternate-runtime execution of a hidden obfuscated blob at install time delivers attacker-controlled code into every installer's environment.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
